# NEAR OutLayer — Full Documentation

> Verifiable compute and custody for AI agents, on NEAR. An agent gets a TEE-held wallet that signs for NEAR, EVM and Solana without a key ever leaving the enclave, spends it under a policy its owner sets, and calls priced connectors — named operations that run inside that same enclave. The compute layer is also callable directly: you build a WASI program, publish the .wasm named by its sha256, and OutLayer runs it inside an Intel TDX enclave and returns the result signed by the enclave — from a NEAR smart contract or over HTTPS. Agents also get encrypted secrets and persistent storage.

Two integration modes. **On-chain:** a NEAR contract calls `request_execution` and receives the result in a callback. **Web2:** a backend calls `POST https://api.outlayer.ai/call/{project_owner}/{project_name}` over HTTPS.

**API base URL is `https://api.outlayer.ai`** — the `api.` subdomain. `https://app.outlayer.ai` is the dashboard and docs site and serves no API. Testnet API base is `https://testnet-api.outlayer.ai`.

HTTPS authentication is either a payment key (`X-Payment-Key: {owner}:{nonce}:{secret}`) or a trial worker key (`Authorization: Bearer wk_...`). There is no `X-API-Key` header.

Mainnet contract: `outlayer.near`. Testnet contract: `outlayer.testnet`. NEAR RPC: `https://rpc.mainnet.fastnear.com` / `https://rpc.testnet.fastnear.com`.

Full text of every document below is available in one fetch at https://app.outlayer.ai/llms-full.txt.

This file inlines every developer-facing document in the OutLayer repository.
For a link index instead, fetch https://app.outlayer.ai/llms.txt.

# NEAR OutLayer

**Verifiable compute and custody for AI agents, on NEAR**

An agent gets a multi-chain wallet whose keys are derived and used inside an Intel TDX enclave, spends it under a policy its owner sets, and calls priced **connectors** — named operations like `send_email` or `pay_invoice` — that run inside that same enclave. Keys and the code that uses them never end up in different trust zones.

The same compute layer is callable directly: a NEAR smart contract can request an execution and resume on the verified result, and a web2 backend can call it over HTTPS. Every execution produces a TDX attestation quote whose signature chains to Intel's root certificate, binding the result to the WASM hash, the input and the measured worker that ran it.

What the operator can and cannot do today — including the governance keys OutLayer still holds at this stage — is stated in [docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md).

## Quick Links

- **Dashboard & Docs**: [app.outlayer.ai](https://app.outlayer.ai) (no API is served from this host)
- **HTTPS API (mainnet)**: `https://api.outlayer.ai` → `POST /call/{owner}/{project}`
- **HTTPS API (testnet)**: `https://testnet-api.outlayer.ai` → `POST /call/{owner}/{project}`
- **Contract**: `outlayer.near` (mainnet) / `outlayer.testnet` (testnet)
- **API reference**: [API.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/API.md) — endpoints, base URLs, authentication
- **For AI coding assistants**: [llms.txt](https://app.outlayer.ai/llms.txt) — link index, or [llms-full.txt](https://app.outlayer.ai/llms-full.txt) for every doc in a single fetch
- **Production App**: [near.email](https://near.email) — blockchain-native email built on OutLayer

## How It Works

1. A NEAR smart contract (or HTTPS client) submits a computation request naming the code: a registered project, or a WASM file by URL and sha256
2. A TEE worker picks up the task, fetches the WASM binary, checks its sha256 and executes it under the request's resource limits
3. The result is returned on-chain (via yield/resume) or in the HTTPS response, together with an attestation record

The contract also accepts a GitHub repository and commit as a source. Building from GitHub is off unless the operator enables it (`BUILDS_ENABLED` on the coordinator, default off); where it is on, builds run on separate compile workers outside the TEE, in Docker. The TEE workers that execute code and receive secrets never compile.

## Project Structure

```
outlayer/
├── contract/              # Main NEAR contract (outlayer.near)
├── register-contract/     # TEE worker registration contract (5-measurement TDX verification)
├── keystore-dao-contract/ # DAO governance for keystore registration (dao.outlayer.near)
├── vault-contract/        # Per-customer vault contract
├── worker/                # Execution workers (Rust + Tokio, wasmtime runtime)
├── keystore-worker/       # Key derivation, signing and secrets decryption (Rust, runs in TEE)
├── sdk/outlayer/          # Rust SDK for WASI apps (crate `outlayer`)
├── connectors/            # Connectors (public ones in-tree, pro ones as private submodules)
├── wasi-examples/         # Example WASI projects and the local test runner
├── self-hosted-scheduler/ # Scheduler for autonomous agents (submodule)
├── deploy/                # Self-hosted TDX deployment tooling
├── docker/                # Docker configurations
├── scripts/               # Deployment & utility scripts
└── tests/                 # Integration tests
```

Separate repositories:

| Component | Repository |
|-----------|------------|
| Coordinator (task queue, HTTPS API, PostgreSQL + Redis) | private: `out-layer/coordinator` |
| Dashboard (web UI + documentation) | [out-layer/dashboard](https://github.com/out-layer/dashboard) |
| CLI | [out-layer/outlayer-cli](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer-cli) |
| TEE challenge-response auth | [out-layer/shared-tee-helpers](https://github.com/out-layer/shared-tee-helpers) |
| TypeScript SDK | [out-layer/sdk-js](https://github.com/out-layer/sdk-js) |

## Two Integration Modes

### Blockchain (NEAR Smart Contracts)

Your contract calls `request_execution` on `outlayer.near`, attaching NEAR for compute. The result comes back via NEAR's yield/resume mechanism. Best for on-chain workflows that need verified computation.

```rust
// In your NEAR contract
#[ext_contract(ext_outlayer)]
trait OutLayer {
    fn request_execution(
        &mut self,
        source: ExecutionSource,
        resource_limits: Option<ResourceLimits>,
        input_data: Option<String>,
        secrets_ref: Option<SecretsReference>,
        response_format: Option<ResponseFormat>,
        payer_account_id: Option<AccountId>,
        params: Option<RequestParams>,
    );
}
```

A request without `resource_limits` only compiles and runs nothing — pass `{}` to take the defaults. See [contract/README.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/contract/README.md).

### HTTPS API (Web2 Apps)

Call the API directly with a payment key. Best for web apps, bots, and services that need off-chain computation without a smart contract.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.outlayer.ai/call/alice.near/my-project \
  -H "X-Payment-Key: alice.near:1:your_secret_key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": {"prompt": "Hello"}}'
```

## Security Model

- **Intel TDX**: Hardware memory encryption and isolation — the host operator cannot read TEE memory
- **5-Measurement Verification**: Workers are registered only when all 5 TDX measurements (MRTD + RTMR0-3) match an approved set, so a dev/debug image fails attestation even when the application matches
- **Sigstore build provenance**: The worker and keystore Docker images are built by GitHub Actions with Sigstore-backed build-provenance attestations, so an image digest can be traced to the source commit it was built from
- **No builds in the TEE**: TEE execution workers run a WASM binary whose sha256 they measure and report to the keystore with every secret decryption; they run no build scripts
- **Stage caveats**: governance currently runs on single keys held by OutLayer (DAO full-access key, owner-only measurement approval, contracts upgraded by key) — see [docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md#governance-at-this-stage)

## Development

The coordinator is a private repository, so the full stack (coordinator + workers + keystore) cannot be run from this repository alone. What you can do from here:

- **Build and test the contracts** — `cd contract && ./build.sh` (uses `cargo near build`); the same for `register-contract/`, `keystore-dao-contract/`, `vault-contract/`
- **Build and unit-test the worker and keystore** — `cargo build` / `cargo test` in `worker/` and `keystore-worker/`; rebuild the release images to compare digests against the Sigstore attestations
- **Write and test a WASI app locally** — follow [wasi-examples/WASI_TUTORIAL.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/wasi-examples/WASI_TUTORIAL.md) and check the binary with [wasi-examples/wasi-test-runner](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/wasi-examples/wasi-test-runner/README.md)
- **Deploy and call it on the hosted network** — with the [OutLayer CLI](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/CLI.md) against `testnet-api.outlayer.ai` or `api.outlayer.ai`

### Prerequisites

- Rust (each component pins its toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml`)
- `cargo-near` (for contract builds)
- NEAR CLI
- Docker (for reproducible image builds)

# OutLayer API

The OutLayer HTTP API is served by the **coordinator** — the task queue and
gateway that fronts the TEE workers, contracts, and keystore. It exposes the
Agent Custody wallet and the verifiable compute layer — connectors and arbitrary
WASI modules — over plain HTTPS.

## Base URLs (Networks)

| Network | Base URL | Contract |
|---------|----------|----------|
| Mainnet | `https://api.outlayer.ai` | `outlayer.near` |
| Testnet | `https://testnet-api.outlayer.ai` | `outlayer.testnet` |

The paths below are identical on both networks — only the host differs. Pick the
base URL that matches the network your project / wallet is deployed on. The
dashboard host `app.outlayer.ai` serves no API.

> **NEAR Intents is mainnet-only.** Testnet does not run the Intents solver
> network, so the intents-dependent Agent Custody endpoints are **not available
> on testnet**: every `/wallet/v1/intents/*` route, cross-chain gasless
> withdrawals, and all `/wallet/v1/confidential/*` routes. Test those against
> the **mainnet** API only. The rest of the wallet API (address, balance,
> transfer, `call`, `sign-message`, policy, approval) works on both networks.

- **Interactive reference (Scalar UI)**: `https://api.outlayer.ai/docs`
- **OpenAPI 3.1 spec**: `https://api.outlayer.ai/openapi.json` — source of truth at [out-layer/api-spec](https://github.com/out-layer/api-spec); request and response schemas live there
- **TypeScript SDK**: [`@outlayer/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@outlayer/sdk) ([source](https://github.com/out-layer/sdk-js))

## Authentication

| Header | Used by | Meaning |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `X-Payment-Key: owner:nonce:secret` | `/call`, `/calls/{id}`, `/payment-keys/balance`, `/subscription/*` | A payment key: a funded key, a subscription, or the wallet's trial key |
| `Authorization: Bearer wk_...` or `Bearer near:...` | All wallet endpoints, `POST /trial-key`, `GET /calls/{id}` | Wallet API key, or a deterministic wallet's NEAR signature. It runs the wallet and does not pay: on `/call` alone it is refused as `401 wk_is_not_a_payer` |
| `X-Wallet-Id` | `/call` to a connector that acts on the wallet | The paying key's own wallet (`wallet_id` from `GET /wallet/v1/address`); without it the run has no wallet |
| _(none)_ | `/register`, public read endpoints | No auth |

> Only `X-Payment-Key` or `Authorization: Bearer wk_...` / `near:...` are
> accepted for authenticated calls. There is no `X-API-Key` header.

## Execution API

| Method | Endpoint | Auth | Description |
|--------|----------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/call/{owner}/{project}` | `X-Payment-Key` | Execute a project's WASI module. Body: `{"input": …, "secrets_ref"?, "secrets_refs"?, "async"?, "version_key"?, "resource_limits"?}`. `secrets_refs` names several secret rows in order (at most 5; not with `secrets_ref`; the project's manifest must say `"secrets_refs": true`): each opens for the caller as one does, their variables join (a name set differently by two rows refuses the run), and a task may be opened for the owner of any of them; refused on a connector that reads the wallet owner's policy row (Polymarket, Hyperliquid), which no other row joins. Sync by default; `"async": true` returns a `call_id` |
| GET | `/calls/{call_id}` | `X-Payment-Key` of the calling key, or `Bearer wk_` of the wallet that owns it | Poll a `pending` call: an async one, or a sync one the API restarted during |
| GET | `/payment-keys/balance` | `X-Payment-Key` | The key's balance |
| GET | `/subscription/status` | `X-Payment-Key` | What a key has left — for a trial key, `trial.calls_left` |
| POST | `/subscription/purchase` | `X-Payment-Key` | Turn balance already on the key into subscription allowance |
| PUT | `/subscription/notifications` | `X-Payment-Key` | Where to warn the owner about allowance and expiry |
| POST | `/trial-key` | `Bearer wk_...` / `near:...` | Claim the wallet's trial key: an allowance for connector calls only, with an expiry; the key is derived and can be read again below |
| GET | `/wallet/v1/payment-key` | `Bearer wk_...` / `near:...` | The wallet's nonce-0 key (trial or sponsored), derived again; only the credential that claimed it reads it |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/sponsorship` | `Bearer wk_...` / `near:...` | Redeem a sponsor code (`spn_…`): a subscription, paid by the sponsor, on the nonce-0 key |

Optional execution headers: `X-Compute-Limit` (max compute budget in
stablecoin minimal units), `X-Attached-Deposit` (payment forwarded to the
project author, read by the WASM via the `USD_PAYMENT` env var; never honoured
for a trial or other granted key).

## Agent Custody Wallet API

Per-agent wallets whose keys are derived inside the keystore TEE from a master
secret issued by the NEAR MPC network. All endpoints except `/register` require
`Authorization: Bearer wk_...` (or `Bearer near:...`).

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| POST | `/register` | Register a wallet, get API key and the trial offer (no auth) |
| GET | `/wallet/v1/balance` | Balance (NEAR or FT), per chain |
| GET | `/wallet/v1/address` | Address for any supported chain |
| GET | `/wallet/v1/tokens` | List supported tokens |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/transfer` | Transfer NEAR / FT |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/call` | Call a NEAR smart contract |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/sign-message` | NEP-413 message signing |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/auth-sign` | OutLayer NEAR-key auth signature (`{purpose, seed, vault_id?}`) |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/evm/sign-message` · `/evm/sign-transaction` · `/evm/sign-typed-data` | EVM signing |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/solana/sign-message` · `/solana/sign-transaction` | Solana signing |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/intents/deposit` | Deposit FT into Intents balance · **mainnet only** |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/intents/withdraw` | Withdrawal — same-chain (native NEAR / NEP-141) or cross-chain (gasless); `/dry-run` available · **mainnet only** |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/intents/transfer` | Transfer inside Intents · **mainnet only** |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/intents/swap` | Swap tokens via Intents; `/swap/quote` for a quote · **mainnet only** |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/intents/deposit/cross-chain` | Cross-chain deposit via 1Click (alias `/wallet/v1/deposit-intent`); `/cross-chain/status` + `/cross-chain/list` available · **mainnet only** |
| POST/GET | `/wallet/v1/limit-orders` | Create / list limit orders (via 1Click); `/{id}`, `/{id}/cancel`, `/cancel-all` |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/create-payment-key` | A key with money on it — no call limit (USDC or NEAR deposit) |
| GET | `/wallet/v1/policy` | The wallet's policy |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/sign-policy` · `/encrypt-policy` | Prepare a policy for storing on chain (spend limits, allowlists) |
| GET/POST | `/wallet/v1/approval/{id}` · `/approve/{id}` · `/reject/{id}` · `/pending_approvals` | Multisig approval flow |
| PUT/DELETE | `/wallet/v1/api-key` · `/api-key/{key_hash}` | Register a delegate `wk_` key (for a sub-agent wallet by seed, or for a deterministic wallet by NEAR signature) / revoke one |
| GET | `/wallet/v1/requests` · `/requests/{id}` | Request list / status |
| GET | `/wallet/v1/audit` | Audit log |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/delete` | Delete wallet |

### Confidential Intents (private balances)

**Mainnet only** — built on NEAR Intents, so unavailable on the testnet API.

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| POST | `/wallet/v1/confidential/shield` | Shield funds into the private shard (alias `/wallet/v1/confidential/deposit`) |
| GET | `/wallet/v1/confidential/balance` | Private balance |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/confidential/transfer` | Private transfer |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/confidential/swap` | Private swap; `/swap/quote` for a quote |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/confidential/withdraw` | Withdraw (incl. native NEAR); `/dry-run` available |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/confidential/unshield` | Move back to public balance |
| POST | `/wallet/v1/confidential/deposit/cross-chain` | Cross-chain deposit into the confidential shard, quote-only: returns a deposit address (alias `/wallet/v1/confidential/deposit-intent`) |

### Payment Checks (gasless agent-to-agent payments)

`/wallet/v1/payment-check/{create,batch-create,claim,reclaim,peek,status,list}`
— see [docs/PAYMENT_CHECKS.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/PAYMENT_CHECKS.md).

## Public (read-only, no auth)

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| GET | `/health` | Health check |
| GET | `/public/pricing` | Current pricing |
| GET | `/public/stats` · `/public/workers` | Network stats / live workers |
| GET | `/public/connectors` · `/public/connectors/{id}/describe` | Connector catalogue / one connector's operations |
| GET / POST | `/public/storage/get` · `/public/storage/batch` | Read public (unencrypted) project storage |
| GET | `/public/payment-keys/{owner}/{nonce}/balance` · `/usage` | Payment key balance / usage |
| GET | `/public/project-earnings/{owner}` · `/public/users/{account}/earnings` | Earnings (read) |
| GET | `/attestations/by-call/{call_id}` · `/by-tx/{tx_hash}` · `/by-request/{request_id}` | Attestation record of one execution |
| GET | `/public/collateral` | Intel TDX collateral for verifying an attestation |
| GET | `/vrf/pubkey` | VRF public key (for on-chain verification) |

## Source availability and trust

**The coordinator (this API) is closed source.** It is the task queue, WASM
cache, payment accounting and HTTPS gateway. It cannot read TEE memory, forge
an attestation, or produce an execution result that passes attestation without
a registered worker having computed it.

It is **not** a stateless proxy, and for agent custody it is a trusted
component:

- it authenticates wallet API keys (it stores only SHA-256 hashes of `wk_` keys);
- it keeps usage counters, pending approvals and a readable copy of wallet
  policies in PostgreSQL — cumulative (daily/hourly/monthly) limits are counted
  here, outside the enclave;
- for swaps, cross-chain withdrawals, confidential transfers, limit orders and
  payment checks it supplies the intents message the enclave signs.

The keystore TEE reads the wallet's policy from the chain before signing, and
enforces per-transaction limits, multisig and freeze inside the enclave. The
exact split, and the governance keys OutLayer holds at this stage, are in
[docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md).

**The components that run in or govern the TEE are open source:**

- **Workers** — execute WASI modules inside Intel TDX TEEs ([worker/](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/worker/))
- **Contracts** — `outlayer.near` and friends ([contract/](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/contract/),
  [register-contract/](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/register-contract/),
  [keystore-dao-contract/](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/keystore-dao-contract/), [vault-contract/](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/vault-contract/))
- **Keystore worker** — key derivation, signing and secrets decryption inside the TEE ([keystore-worker/](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/keystore-worker/))
- **Libraries / SDKs** — [sdk/outlayer/](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/sdk/outlayer/) (Rust, on crates.io as
  [`outlayer`](https://crates.io/crates/outlayer)),
  [`@outlayer/sdk`](https://github.com/out-layer/sdk-js) (TypeScript),
  [shared-tee-helpers](https://github.com/out-layer/shared-tee-helpers)
  (TEE challenge-response auth)

See [README.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/README.md#security-model) and
[WORKER_ATTESTATION.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/WORKER_ATTESTATION.md).

# OutLayer CLI

Command-line tool for deploying, running, and managing OutLayer agents.

```bash
outlayer login                                              # Import NEAR full access key
outlayer create my-agent                                    # Create project from template
outlayer upload my_agent.wasm                               # Publish the built .wasm to FastFS
outlayer deploy my-agent <FastFS URL>                       # Deploy it to OutLayer
outlayer run alice.near/my-agent '{"command": "hello"}'     # Execute agent
```

## Install

```bash
# Prebuilt binary (macOS / Linux)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/out-layer/outlayer-cli/main/install.sh | sh

# From crates.io (requires Rust 1.86+)
cargo install outlayer-cli

# From GitHub source
cargo install --git https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer-cli

# Update an installed binary to the latest GitHub release
outlayer update
```

Prebuilt binaries for macOS (ARM/x86), Linux (x86/ARM) and Windows (x86) are on the
[Releases](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer-cli/releases) page. `install.sh`
installs to `/usr/local/bin` (override with `INSTALL_DIR`).

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. Login (prompts for Account ID and Private Key)
outlayer login              # mainnet
outlayer login testnet      # testnet

# 2. Create a new agent
outlayer create my-agent                     # basic template (stdin/stdout)
outlayer create my-agent --template contract # with OutLayer SDK (VRF, storage, RPC)
cd my-agent

# 3. Edit src/main.rs, build, publish the .wasm and deploy it
./build.sh                                   # writes out/my_agent.wasm (Cargo name: '-' becomes '_')
outlayer upload out/my_agent.wasm
outlayer deploy my-agent <FastFS URL printed by upload>

# 4. Create a payment key for HTTPS calls, and fund it
outlayer keys create
outlayer keys topup 1 --usd 1

# 5. Run your agent (HTTPS when PAYMENT_KEY is set, otherwise on-chain)
export PAYMENT_KEY=$(outlayer keys show 1)
outlayer run alice.near/my-agent '{"command": "hello"}'
```

OutLayer runs published `.wasm` builds: build locally, `outlayer upload`, `outlayer deploy`.
The CLI does not deploy from a GitHub repository.

## Authentication

### Login

```bash
outlayer login                        # mainnet (default)
outlayer login testnet                # testnet
outlayer login --wallet-key wk_...    # custody wallet API key instead of a NEAR key
```

`outlayer login` prompts for an Account ID and an ed25519 private key (`ed25519:...`)
and writes both to `~/.outlayer/{network}/credentials.json`. The private key is kept
in that file in plain text.

`--wallet-key` logs in as a custody wallet: the account and public key come from the
wallet, the `wk_` key is stored in `credentials.json`, and contract calls are signed
through the wallet API. `vault` commands refuse a wallet-key login.

```bash
outlayer whoami             # Account, network, contract, public key, auth type
outlayer logout             # Delete stored credentials for the active network
outlayer about              # Banner and version
```

### Network

Each command picks its network in this order:

1. `OUTLAYER_NETWORK` (`mainnet` or `testnet`)
2. `network` in `./outlayer.toml`
3. `~/.outlayer/default-network`, written by `login`
4. the only network that has a `credentials.json`
5. `mainnet`

`login` takes its network from its argument. `logout`, `whoami` and `create` skip step 2.

| Network | Contract | API |
|---------|----------|-----|
| mainnet | `outlayer.near` | `https://api.outlayer.ai` |
| testnet | `outlayer.testnet` | `https://testnet-api.outlayer.ai` |

## Commands

### Project Workflow

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer create <name>` | Create project from template (basic) in `./<name>/` |
| `outlayer create <name> --template contract` | Create with OutLayer SDK (VRF, storage, RPC) |
| `outlayer create <name> --dir /path` | Create in `/path/<name>/` |
| `outlayer deploy <name> <wasm-url>` | Deploy a published .wasm (the FastFS URL `outlayer upload` prints, or any https URL): creates the project, or adds a version and activates it |
| `outlayer deploy <name> <wasm-url> --no-activate` | Add a version without activating it (a new project's first version is always active) |
| `outlayer deploy <name> <wasm-url> --hash <sha256>` | Skip downloading the file to compute its hash |
| `outlayer run <project> [input]` | Execute agent (HTTPS or on-chain) |
| `outlayer projects [account]` | List projects for an account (default: logged-in account) |
| `outlayer status` | Active version of the project in `./outlayer.toml` |
| `outlayer status <call_id>` | Poll an HTTPS call (uses `PAYMENT_KEY`) |

`deploy` attaches 0.1 NEAR for storage; the contract refunds what it does not use.

A version is a published `.wasm`, named by its sha256, so what a caller runs and
pays for cannot change under that version afterwards — a repository can change
under the same name and commit history can be rewritten. `deploy` computes the
hash from the URL (or takes `--hash`); the worker refuses a file whose bytes do
not match it. For a reproducible build — the same pinned Docker image, the same
hash every time — use `scripts/build_github_wasm.sh --dir ./my-project --target
wasm32-wasip2` from the [OutLayer repository](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer).

### Run

```bash
# Uses HTTPS when a payment key is found, else on-chain NEAR
outlayer run alice.near/my-agent '{"command": "hello"}'
outlayer run alice.near/my-agent --input request.json             # input from file
echo '{"command": "hello"}' | outlayer run alice.near/my-agent    # input from stdin
outlayer run alice.near/my-agent '{"command": "heavy"}' --async   # async (HTTPS only)
outlayer run alice.near/my-agent '{}' --version <sha256>          # specific version

# Attach secrets (both flags together)
outlayer run alice.near/my-agent '{}' --secrets-profile default --secrets-account alice.near

# Run a published WASM URL directly (always on-chain)
outlayer run --wasm https://main.fastfs.io/alice.near/outlayer.near/<sha256>.wasm '{"cmd": "hi"}'
outlayer run --wasm https://example.com/file.wasm --hash <sha256> '{}'
```

With no input, `run` reads stdin when it is piped, else sends `{}`.

**HTTPS mode** — a project run when a payment key is found: the `PAYMENT_KEY`
environment variable, else a `PAYMENT_KEY=` line in `./.env`. Keys made by
`keys create` are not picked up on their own; `outlayer keys show <nonce>` prints one.

```
POST https://api.outlayer.ai/call/{owner}/{project}
X-Payment-Key: owner:nonce:secret
X-Compute-Limit: <--compute-limit>          (if given)
X-Attached-Deposit: <--deposit>             (if given)
Content-Type: application/json

{"input": ..., "async": false, "version_key": ..., "secrets_ref": {...}}
```

Both headers are amounts in the stablecoin's minimal units (6 decimals: `1000000` = $1).
`--compute-limit` is the call's compute budget and `--deposit` a payment to the project
owner, for example `--deposit 10000` for $0.01. The value is sent as given; the API reads
only a whole number, so a decimal such as `0.01` attaches nothing.

**On-chain mode** — every `--wasm` run, and a project run with no payment key: calls
`request_execution` on the contract with the estimated cost as the NEAR deposit, 128 MB of
memory and 10 seconds. `--compute-limit` is the instruction limit (default 1,000,000,000).
`--async` is refused; `--deposit` is not used.

### Secrets

Encrypted client-side, decrypted only inside the TEE.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer secrets set '{"KEY":"val"}'` | Encrypt and store secrets (JSON, overwrites) |
| `outlayer secrets update '{"KEY":"val"}'` | Merge with existing (preserves PROTECTED_*) |
| `outlayer secrets set --generate PROTECTED_X:hex32` | Generate protected secret in TEE |
| `outlayer secrets access --access <cond>` | Change who may read a stored secret; the value stays |
| `outlayer secrets list` | List stored secrets (metadata only) |
| `outlayer secrets delete` | Delete secrets for a profile |
| `outlayer secrets set-for-agent '{"KEY":"val"}' --project <owner>/<name>` | Leave a secret for a custody agent to use with one connector |
| `outlayer secrets delete-for-agent --project <owner>/<name>` | Remove it and take the storage deposit back |

```bash
# Set secrets (JSON object, overwrites existing)
outlayer secrets set '{"API_KEY":"sk-...","DB_URL":"postgres://..."}'
outlayer secrets set '{"API_KEY":"sk-..."}' --project alice.near/my-agent
outlayer secrets set '{"API_KEY":"sk-..."}' --wasm-hash <sha256>   # the row a raw WASM URL run reads under
outlayer secrets set '{"SIGNING_KEY":"..."}' --project alice.near/oracle --build <sha256>   # locked to one build
outlayer secrets access --project alice.near/oracle --access whitelist:alice.near --build <new sha256>   # move to the next release

# Named profile (default: "default")
outlayer secrets set '{"KEY":"val"}' --profile production

# Bind to a per-customer vault
outlayer secrets set '{"KEY":"val"}' --vault-id vault.alice.near

# Generate protected secrets in TEE (values never visible)
outlayer secrets set --generate PROTECTED_MASTER_KEY:hex32
outlayer secrets set '{"API_KEY":"sk-..."}' --generate PROTECTED_DB:hex64   # mixed

# Access control
outlayer secrets set '{"KEY":"val"}' --access allow-all                      # everyone who names it
outlayer secrets set '{"KEY":"val"}' --access whitelist:alice.near,bob.near
outlayer secrets set '{"KEY":"val"}' --access whitelist:alice.near,agent.near@2026-12-01T00:00:00Z   # a grant that lapses
# Without --access: a row that exists keeps its condition; a new project row admits only you;
# a new hash row admits everyone.

# Direct calls only: the account that calls the contract must be a reader the condition names
outlayer secrets set '{"SIGNING_KEY":"..."}' --project alice.near/oracle --direct
outlayer secrets access --project alice.near/oracle --direct --via dao.sputnik-dao.near   # and through this contract
outlayer secrets access --project alice.near/oracle --drop-callers                        # remove the rule

# Update (merge with existing, preserves all PROTECTED_* variables)
outlayer secrets update '{"NEW_KEY":"val"}' --project alice.near/my-agent
outlayer secrets update --generate PROTECTED_NEW:ed25519

# Generation types: hex16, hex32, hex64, ed25519, ed25519_seed, password, password:N

# List / delete
outlayer secrets list
outlayer secrets delete --project alice.near/my-agent
outlayer secrets delete --profile production
```

Default accessor: `--project` auto-resolved from `outlayer.toml` if present.

A deadline in a whitelist entry (`account@...`) is UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` or
`YYYY-MM-DD`; after it the entry no longer admits.

A row is bound to a project (`--project`) or to a build (`--wasm-hash`). A row
bound to a repository is listed by `secrets list` and can be deleted
(`secrets delete --repo <repo> --branch <branch>`); nothing new is stored,
updated or re-scoped for a repository.

`--build <sha256>` locks a project's row to one build: the
condition becomes `And[<access>, WasmHash(hash)]` (or the `WasmHash` leaf alone
under `allow-all`), and the keystore admits only a run whose bytes hash to it.
A rebuild is refused with the build named. The value stays; `secrets access
--build <new sha256>` moves the row to the next release without re-storing, so
a generated `PROTECTED_` key keeps its value — and with no `--access` it keeps
the readers the row already has. `--wasm-hash` is different: it is the accessor
a raw WASM URL run reads under, not a lock on a project row.

On a locked row, `--access …` (in `set` or `access`) is refused: an explicit
condition replaces the stored one, lock included. Pass `--build` to keep it
locked, or `--drop-build` to remove the lock deliberately. The hash is
**Executed binary** in an execution's details on the dashboard. A row that carries
a calling-account rule (`--direct` / `--via`) is protected the same way: replacing
its condition needs `--direct`, `--via` or `--drop-callers`.

`set-for-agent` stores a secret for a **custody agent** to use with somebody else's
connector. It takes the agent's wallet key (`--api-key wk_...` or `OUTLAYER_WALLET_KEY`),
seals the value to the agent's key and stores it under the agent's account. Scope it with
`--project <owner>/<name>` or `--wasm-hash <sha256>`. The logged-in account pays the
storage deposit unless `--agent-pays` is given (the agent's wallet then needs ~0.11 NEAR);
`--vault-id` refuses unless the secret lands under that vault.

### Payment Keys

Payment keys pay for HTTPS API calls.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer keys create` | Create a new payment key (attaches 0.1 NEAR for storage) |
| `outlayer keys create --project <owner>/<name>` | Let the key pay only for that project; `owner/*` for all of one owner's projects; repeatable |
| `outlayer keys show <nonce>` | Print a key this machine created |
| `outlayer keys list` | List keys with balances |
| `outlayer keys balance <nonce>` | Balance, spent, reserved, initial |
| `outlayer keys topup <nonce> --usd <amount>` | Top up with the stablecoin (any network) |
| `outlayer keys topup <nonce> <amount>` | Top up with NEAR, swapped to USDC through NEAR Intents (mainnet only, minimum 0.035 NEAR) |
| `outlayer keys delete <nonce>` | Delete key: the storage deposit is refunded, the remaining balance is forfeited |
| `outlayer keys trial-key [--api-key wk_...]` | Print a custody wallet's nonce-0 key (trial or sponsored); it is derived, so it is read again rather than stored |
| `outlayer redeem <spn_...> [--api-key wk_...] [--payment-key owner:0:key]` | Redeem a sponsor code: a subscription on the wallet's nonce-0 key, paid by the sponsor; stdout is the key. `--payment-key` sends a nonce-0 key issued at random, which cannot be read again, as the proof that binds it; the answer is the derived key that replaces it |

```bash
outlayer keys create
# Payment key created (nonce: 1)
# It pays for any project.
# alice.near:1:a1b2c3d4e5f6...              <- stdout
# Saved to ~/.outlayer/mainnet/payment-keys.json (owner-only). Read it back with: outlayer keys show 1
# Add a balance before using it: outlayer keys topup 1 --usd 1

outlayer keys topup 1 --usd 5
outlayer keys list
outlayer keys balance 1
outlayer keys delete 2
```

A key exists in plain text only on the machine that created it:
`keys create` writes it to `~/.outlayer/{network}/payment-keys.json` (mode 0600)
before sending the transaction, and the chain holds it encrypted for the keystore
only. A key that is not in that file cannot be recovered.

A top-up shows in the balance once the worker has processed it, not instantly.

A deleted key's unspent balance is not refunded and does not move to another
key. Deleting it does not free its nonce: the contract refuses a new key there,
and `keys create` takes the next nonce from the contract
(`get_next_payment_key_nonce`).

### Payment Checks (agent-to-agent)

Token transfers between custody wallets through ephemeral NEAR Intents accounts —
mainnet only. Every `checks` command takes the wallet key (`--api-key wk_...` or
`OUTLAYER_WALLET_KEY`); amounts are in the token's smallest units.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer checks create <token> <amount> [--memo <text>] [--expires-in <secs>]` | Create a check; prints its `check_key` to hand over |
| `outlayer checks batch-create --file <path>` | Create checks from a JSON array of `{token, amount, memo?, expires_in?}` |
| `outlayer checks claim <check_key> [--amount <n>]` | Claim a check (full, or partial with `--amount`) |
| `outlayer checks reclaim <check_id> [--amount <n>]` | Take back unclaimed funds (full or partial) |
| `outlayer checks status <check_id>` | Status of one check |
| `outlayer checks list [--status <s>] [--limit <n>]` | List checks (`unclaimed`, `claimed`, `partially_claimed`, `reclaimed`, `expired`; default limit 50) |
| `outlayer checks peek <check_key>` | Balance of a check before claiming it |
| `outlayer checks sign-message <message> <recipient> [--nonce <base64>]` | NEP-413 signature by the wallet, for an external service |

### Vaults

Per-customer sovereign vaults ([VAULTS.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/VAULTS.md)).
Every `vault` command that signs needs a NEAR full-access key login, as the vault's parent account.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer vault init [--name vault] [--parent <account>] [--exit-window 24h] [--webhook-url <https url>]` | Deploy a vault at `<name>.<parent>`, verify it and register it |
| `outlayer vault resume <account>` | Finish an interrupted `init` |
| `outlayer vault status <account>` | Parent, exit window, recovery, registered TEE keys |
| `outlayer vault verify <account>` | `is_vault_verified` and further checks |
| `outlayer vault initiate-recovery <account>` | Cessation-triggered recovery (requires the DAO's `is_ceased`) |
| `outlayer vault initiate-unilateral-recovery <account>` | Parent-only recovery after the exit window |
| `outlayer vault finalize-recovery <account> <ed25519:pubkey>` | Finish a recovery: the key becomes the vault's only full-access key and the TEE keys are removed |
| `outlayer vault set-exit-window <account> <window>` | Change the exit window for future recoveries |
| `outlayer vault unlocked-add-key <account> <ed25519:pubkey> [--full-access]` | After a recovery, add a key (default: function-call key with 1 NEAR allowance) |

### Upload (FastFS)

Upload files to on-chain storage via NEAR transactions.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer upload <file>` | Upload file to FastFS |
| `outlayer upload <file> --receiver <account>` | Custom receiver (default: the OutLayer contract, `outlayer.near` / `outlayer.testnet`) |
| `outlayer upload <file> --mime-type <type>` | Override MIME type (default: from the file extension) |

```bash
outlayer upload ./target/wasm32-wasip2/release/my_agent.wasm
#   SHA256: <sha256>
#   ...
# FastFS URL: https://main.fastfs.io/alice.near/outlayer.near/<sha256>.wasm
```

The URL is `https://<host>/<sender>/<receiver>/<sha256>.<ext>`; the host is
`main.fastfs.io` on mainnet and `test.fastfs.io` on testnet. Files over 1 MiB are
sent in 1 MiB chunks, one transaction each. A wallet-key login uploads through the
wallet API.

> **Note:** FastFS upload transactions **fail on purpose** with "Exceeded the prepaid gas": gas is set to 1, because no contract code needs to run — the FastFS indexer reads the file from the transaction arguments regardless of execution status. The file is served at its FastFS URL once the indexer has picked it up; a chunked file, once every chunk is indexed.

### Versions

Read the project from `./outlayer.toml`.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer versions` | List project versions (up to 50; keys shortened to 10 characters) |
| `outlayer versions activate <key>` | Switch active version (`<key>` is the full sha256) |
| `outlayer versions remove <key>` | Remove a version |

### Earnings

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer earnings` | View blockchain + HTTPS earnings |
| `outlayer earnings withdraw` | Withdraw blockchain earnings to the logged-in account |
| `outlayer earnings history` | View earnings history (default: 20 entries) |
| `outlayer earnings history --source blockchain` | Filter by source: `blockchain` or `https` |
| `outlayer earnings history --limit 50` | Custom limit |

### Logs

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `outlayer logs` | Execution history of the key `payment_key_nonce` in `outlayer.toml` names |
| `outlayer logs --nonce 2` | History for a specific key |
| `outlayer logs --limit 50` | Custom number of entries (default: 20) |

## Configuration

### Files

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `~/.outlayer/{network}/credentials.json` | Account, public key, and the private key or `wk_` key |
| `~/.outlayer/{network}/payment-keys.json` | Payment keys this machine created (mode 0600) |
| `~/.outlayer/default-network` | Network chosen by the last `login` |

### Project Config

`outlayer.toml` in your project root (created by `outlayer create`). The fields the CLI reads:

```toml
network = "mainnet"        # network for commands run in this directory

[project]
name = "my-agent"          # status, versions, and the default secrets accessor
owner = "alice.near"

[run]
payment_key_nonce = 1      # outlayer logs; add it yourself
```

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `OUTLAYER_HOME` | Config directory (default: `~/.outlayer`) |
| `OUTLAYER_NETWORK` | Network: `mainnet` or `testnet` |
| `OUTLAYER_RPC_URL` | NEAR RPC endpoint for the active network (default: `https://rpc.mainnet.near.org` / `https://test.rpc.fastnear.com`) |
| `PAYMENT_KEY` | Payment key for `outlayer run` and `outlayer status <call_id>` (format: `owner:nonce:secret`); also read from a `PAYMENT_KEY=` line in `./.env` |
| `OUTLAYER_WALLET_KEY` | Custody wallet API key (`wk_...`) for `checks`, `redeem`, `keys trial-key`, `secrets set-for-agent` / `delete-for-agent` |

### Global Flags

```bash
outlayer --verbose ...            # also -v; available on all commands
```

## Templates

### basic (default)

Rust + wasm32-wasip2 project: reads JSON from stdin, writes JSON to stdout.

### contract

Rust + wasm32-wasip2 with the `outlayer` SDK crate (VRF, storage, NEAR RPC bindings).

Both include `Cargo.toml`, `src/main.rs`, `build.sh`, `.gitignore`, `skill.md` and
`outlayer.toml`. `build.sh` builds for `wasm32-wasip2` and copies the result to
`out/<name>.wasm`, with `-` in the name replaced by `_`.

<!-- source: wasi-examples/README.md -->
> Source: https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/wasi-examples/README.md

# WASI Examples for NEAR OutLayer

Collection of examples and tools for developing WASM modules for NEAR OutLayer platform.

## 📚 Documentation

### [WASI Tutorial](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/wasi-examples/WASI_TUTORIAL.md) - **START HERE**
Complete guide for developing WASI modules:
- WASI Preview 1 vs Preview 2
- Quick start templates
- Input/output patterns
- Requirements and best practices
- Common pitfalls and solutions

### [Test Runner](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/wasi-examples/wasi-test-runner/) - **VALIDATE YOUR MODULE**
Universal tool to test WASM modules for compatibility:
```bash
cd wasi-test-runner
cargo build --release
./target/release/wasi-test --wasm your-app.wasm --input '{"test":"data"}'
```

## 📦 Examples

### [random-example](https://github.com/out-layer/random-example) - WASI P1
Simple random number generator demonstrating:
- ✅ WASI Preview 1 (wasm32-wasip1)
- ✅ Binary format with `main()`
- ✅ JSON input/output via stdin/stdout
- ✅ Random number generation
- ✅ ~111KB binary size

**Use case**: Basic computations, random numbers, simple I/O

### [ai-example](https://github.com/out-layer/ai-example) - WASI P2
HTTP client for AI APIs demonstrating:
- ✅ WASI Preview 2 (wasm32-wasip2)
- ✅ Component model
- ✅ HTTP/HTTPS requests
- ✅ OpenAI-compatible API integration
- ✅ Fuel metering

**Use case**: HTTP requests, API calls, external data fetching

### [oracle-example](https://github.com/out-layer/oracle-example) - WASI P2
On-demand price oracle demonstrating:
- ✅ WASI Preview 2 (wasm32-wasip2)
- ✅ Multiple HTTP sources (CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap, TwelveData)
- ✅ Price aggregation (average, median, weighted)
- ✅ Encrypted API keys via env vars
- ✅ Batch requests (up to 10 tokens)

**Use case**: Decentralized oracles, price feeds, multi-source data aggregation

## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Choose Your WASI Version

**WASI P1** - For simple computations:
```bash
rustup target add wasm32-wasip1
cargo build --target wasm32-wasip1 --release
```

**WASI P2** - For HTTP and advanced I/O:
```bash
rustup target add wasm32-wasip2
cargo build --target wasm32-wasip2 --release
```

### 2. Follow the Pattern

```rust
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::io::{self, Read, Write};

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Input { /* your fields */ }

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Output { /* your fields */ }

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // Read from stdin
    let mut input = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input)?;

    // Parse JSON
    let data: Input = serde_json::from_str(&input)?;

    // Process...
    let result = process(data)?;

    // Write to stdout
    let output = Output { result };
    print!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&output)?);
    io::stdout().flush()?;

    Ok(())
}
```

### 3. Test Locally

```bash
# With wasmtime (a P2 component that makes HTTP requests needs -S http)
echo '{"test":"data"}' | wasmtime your-app.wasm
echo '{"test":"data"}' | wasmtime run -S http your-app.wasm

# With test runner (recommended)
cd wasi-test-runner
./target/release/wasi-test --wasm ../your-app.wasm --input '{"test":"data"}'
```

### 4. Deploy to NEAR OutLayer

OutLayer runs a published `.wasm`, named by its sha256. Publish the file you
built and register it as a project version:

```bash
outlayer upload your-app.wasm
# prints SHA256 and: FastFS URL: https://test.fastfs.io/your.testnet/outlayer.testnet/<sha256>.wasm
outlayer deploy your-app <FastFS URL> --target wasm32-wasip1
```

Then call it:

```bash
near call outlayer.testnet request_execution '{
  "source": {
    "Project": {"project_id": "your.testnet/your-app", "version_key": null}
  },
  "resource_limits": {
    "max_instructions": 10000000,
    "max_memory_mb": 128,
    "max_execution_seconds": 60
  },
  "input_data": "{\"test\":\"data\"}"
}' --accountId your.testnet --deposit 0.1
```

## ✅ Requirements Checklist

Before deploying to NEAR OutLayer, ensure:

- ✅ Using `[[bin]]` format (not `[lib]`)
- ✅ Have `fn main()` as entry point
- ✅ Reading from stdin (not args)
- ✅ Writing to stdout (not stderr)
- ✅ Flushing stdout after write
- ✅ Valid JSON on stdout when the caller asks for `Json` (every HTTPS call does)
- ✅ Output within 10 MiB (the worker's stdout capacity)
- ✅ No file access: a run has no filesystem, keep data in memory
- ✅ Built with wasm32-wasip1 or wasm32-wasip2
- ✅ Tested with [test runner](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/tree/main/wasi-examples/wasi-test-runner/)

## 🛠️ Cargo.toml Template

```toml
[package]
name = "your-app"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[[bin]]
name = "your-app"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"

# For WASI P2 only:
# wasi-http-client = "0.2"

[profile.release]
opt-level = "z"  # Optimize for size
lto = true       # Link-time optimization
strip = true     # Strip debug symbols
```

## 🔧 Useful Commands

```bash
# Check binary type
file your-app.wasm

# Check size
ls -lh your-app.wasm

# Test with input file
echo '{"test":"data"}' > input.json
wasmtime your-app.wasm < input.json

# Inspect with wasm-tools
wasm-tools print your-app.wasm | head -50

# For P2 components
wasm-tools component wit your-app.wasm
```

## 🐛 Troubleshooting

### Common Errors

| Error | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| "entry symbol not defined: _initialize" | Use `[[bin]]` instead of `[lib]` |
| "Failed to find _start function" | Add `fn main()` entry point |
| Empty output | Add `io::stdout().flush()?` |
| "not a valid WASI P2 component or WASI P1 module" | Check build target |
| JSON parse error on an HTTPS call | stdout must be one JSON value: no extra prints |

See [WASI_TUTORIAL.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/wasi-examples/WASI_TUTORIAL.md#common-pitfalls) for detailed solutions.

### WASI P1 Examples
- Random number generation
- Hash computation (SHA256, etc.)
- JSON transformation
- Data validation
- Simple calculations
- Text processing

### WASI P2 Examples
- API requests (REST, GraphQL)
- AI/ML inference calls
- Price oracles
- Data aggregation
- Content fetching
- Multi-step workflows
