<!-- source: docs/DETERMINISTIC_WALLETS.md -->
> Source: https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/DETERMINISTIC_WALLETS.md

# Deterministic Wallets via NEAR Signature Auth

## Why this matters

OutLayer wallet keys are derived on demand inside an Intel TDX enclave (the keystore) from a master secret issued by the NEAR MPC network; they are never stored, and no endpoint exports them. At this stage OutLayer still holds governance keys that bear on that guarantee — see [Governance at this stage](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md#governance-at-this-stage).

Deterministic wallets let one NEAR account own any number of wallets for its users without storing a credential per user. The wallet is identified by `(account_id, seed)`, and every request is authenticated by a fresh signature from that account's key.

## Problem

`POST /register` without a body creates a wallet with a random `wk_` API key. A client serving many users must store one `wk_` per user; a leak of that store is a leak of every wallet.

## Solution

Authenticate with a NEAR signature on every request. The coordinator stores no auth secret for these wallets: it checks the signature and that the signing key is a full-access key of the account. The client derives wallet access from its NEAR key + a seed — nothing to store per user.

Key revocation = remove the key from the NEAR account. It takes effect within 60 seconds (the coordinator's access-key cache).

## Use cases

**Web app with OAuth login.** The server holds one NEAR key. A user logs in via Google/GitHub; the server sets `seed = hex(SHA256(provider + ":" + user_id))` and the user has a wallet. No per-user key storage.

**Telegram/Discord bot.** The bot holds one NEAR key in env. For each user, `seed = hex(SHA256(telegram_user_id))`. No per-user DB.

**AI agent spawning sub-agents.** The parent derives a `wk_` key from (its key, seed, index), registers its hash via `PUT /wallet/v1/api-key`, and hands the key string to the sub-agent. The sub-agent uses a plain `Bearer wk_...` — no crypto, works with any HTTP client or LLM framework. The parent can re-derive the key at any time without storage.

All three share one pattern: **one NEAR account, many wallets, no stored per-user secrets, access control through NEAR keys.**

## What every wallet gets

A deterministic wallet is a wallet like any other; every `/wallet/v1/*` endpoint works the same way:

- **Addresses** — the NEAR implicit account, one `0x` address for every EVM chain, and a Solana address, all derived from the wallet (`GET /wallet/v1/address`). Other chains are reached through NEAR Intents.
- **Swaps** — `/wallet/v1/intents/swap` through 1Click, gasless from the intents balance.
- **Cross-chain deposits and withdrawals** — `/wallet/v1/intents/deposit/cross-chain` and `/wallet/v1/intents/withdraw` through 1Click.
- **On-chain calls** — NEAR contract calls (`/wallet/v1/call`).
- **Token transfers** — native NEAR (`/wallet/v1/transfer`) and intents balances (`/wallet/v1/intents/transfer`).
- **Policy engine** — capabilities, limits, whitelists, time windows, rate limit, multisig approval, freeze.
- **Webhooks** — the policy's `webhook_url` receives wallet events.
- **Trial** — a wallet can claim a trial key (`POST /trial-key`) within its first days; the `trial` block of the `POST /register` response states the calls and days.

Intents operations are mainnet only.

## Architecture

```
Client (bot)                    Coordinator                  Keystore (TEE)
   |                                |                            |
   |-- Bearer near:<signed JSON> -->|                            |
   |                                |-- verify ed25519 sig       |
   |                                |-- RPC: full-access key?    |
   |                                |-- derive wallet_id         |
   |                                |-- create row if new        |
   |                                |-- operation -------------->|
   |                                |<-- signature / address ----|
   |<-- result ---------------------|                            |
```

- **Auth** = ed25519 signature verification in the coordinator + a full-access-key check over RPC, cached 60 s.
- **Wallet keys** = derived and used by the keystore, as for every wallet.
- **Coordinator DB** = a `wallet_accounts` row; no auth secret for `Bearer near:`.

## Auth: Bearer token format

One `Authorization` header for every wallet type, told apart by prefix:

```
# Random wallets and delegate keys
Authorization: Bearer wk_a1b2c3d4...

# Deterministic wallets
Authorization: Bearer near:<base64url>
```

The base64url payload (padding optional) is a JSON object:

```json
{
  "account_id": "my-tg-bot.near",
  "seed": "a1b2c3...",
  "pubkey": "ed25519:<base58>",
  "timestamp": 1712000000,
  "signature": "<base58>"
}
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `account_id` | The client's NEAR account |
| `seed` | Which wallet: 1–256 characters of `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` (no `:`) |
| `pubkey` | A **full-access** key of `account_id`, `ed25519:<base58>` (or the key of an implicit account that does not exist on chain yet). A function-call key is refused |
| `timestamp` | Unix seconds, within ±30 s of the coordinator's clock |
| `signature` | Raw ed25519 signature (not NEP-413), base58, of `auth:<seed>:<timestamp>` |
| `vault_id` | Optional. Scopes the wallet to a per-customer vault; the signed message is then `auth:<seed>:<timestamp>:<vault_id>`, and `account_id` must be the vault's parent on chain |

The wallet is created on the first authenticated request; `POST /register` is optional for a `Bearer near:` client.

### Verification

1. base64url-decode → parse JSON; validate `seed`.
2. Rebuild `auth:<seed>:<timestamp>` (`:<vault_id>` appended when present), check the timestamp (±30 s), verify the raw ed25519 signature against `pubkey`.
3. Check that `pubkey` is a full-access key of `account_id`: cached result, otherwise one NEAR RPC call. Both answers are cached for 60 s.
4. With `vault_id`: check the vault is verified on the DAO contract and that `account_id` is its parent.
5. `wallet_id = UUID(SHA256("outlayer:deterministic-wallet-id:" + account_id + ":" + seed [+ "\0vault:" + vault_id])[..16])`.
6. Create the `wallet_accounts` row if it does not exist.

Two timestamp windows:
- ±30 s for `Bearer near:` (every request).
- ±300 s for `POST /register` and `PUT /wallet/v1/api-key` with a NEAR signature in the body (setup steps).

The order the coordinator tries credentials: the worker's internal credential (`X-Internal-Wallet-Auth` + `X-Wallet-Id`, for WASI host functions), then `Bearer near:`, then `Bearer wk_` (looked up by SHA-256 hash).

## POST /register — deterministic path

### Request

```json
{
  "account_id": "my-tg-bot.near",
  "seed": "a1b2c3...",
  "pubkey": "ed25519:<base58>",
  "message": "register:<seed>:<timestamp_sec>",
  "signature": "<base58>"
}
```

Any of these five fields present = deterministic path, and then all five are required. None present = random wallet with a `wk_` key. The deterministic path does not take `vault_id` (400); a vault-scoped deterministic wallet is reached with `Bearer near:` carrying `vault_id`.

### Validation

1. `seed` is 1–256 characters of `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]`.
2. `message` is `register:<seed>:<timestamp>` with the same seed.
3. Timestamp within ±300 s.
4. Raw ed25519 signature (not NEP-413) of `message` verifies against `pubkey`.
5. For a wallet that does not exist yet: `pubkey` is a full-access key of `account_id` (cached 60 s).

`POST /register` is rate-limited per IP.

### Response

```json
{
  "wallet_id": "uuid-string",
  "near_account_id": "hex64-implicit-account",
  "trial": { "available": true, "calls": 50, "days": 7, "claim_url": "POST /trial-key", "scope": "connectors.outlayer.near/*" }
}
```

No `api_key` and no `handoff_url`. Repeating the call returns the same wallet, without `trial`.

## Key rotation

No endpoint needed.

```bash
# 1. Add the new key
near add-key my-tg-bot.near ed25519:NEW_KEY

# 2. Sign with the new key — accepted at once

# 3. Remove the old key
near delete-key my-tg-bot.near ed25519:OLD_KEY

# 4. Within 60 s the cached answer for the old key expires → 401
```

The wallet is `(account_id, seed)`; keys rotate freely.

## What the keystore does

- Derives the wallet's keys (`wallet:{wallet_id}:near`, `:evm`, `:solana`) from the master on demand.
- Evaluates the wallet's policy and signs.

No auth credential for `Bearer near:` is stored anywhere.

## PUT /wallet/v1/api-key — delegate key for sub-agents

Registers the SHA-256 hash (64 hex characters) of a client-derived `wk_` key, creating the wallet it opens if needed. Idempotent. Two auth modes.

### Mode 1: Bearer header (an existing wallet creates a sub-wallet)

An authenticated wallet (`Bearer wk_...` or `Bearer near:...`) creates a sub-wallet. No NEAR signature in the body.

```json
{
  "seed": "sub-task-42",
  "key_hash": "sha256hex64chars..."
}
```

Sub-wallet `wallet_id = deterministic(parent_wallet_id, seed, parent's vault)`. A vault-bound parent's sub-wallets derive from the same vault. No RPC check.

**Ambiguity guard:** a Bearer header together with any of `account_id`, `pubkey`, `message`, `signature` or `vault_id` in the body → 400.

### Mode 2: NEAR signature in the body (a NEAR account, no Bearer header)

```json
{
  "account_id": "parent-agent.near",
  "seed": "sub-task-42",
  "key_hash": "sha256hex64chars...",
  "pubkey": "ed25519:<base58>",
  "message": "api-key:sub-task-42:<timestamp>",
  "signature": "<base58>"
}
```

Timestamp within ±300 s, raw ed25519 signature, and `pubkey` must be a full-access key of `account_id` on every call. Optional `vault_id`: `account_id` must be the vault's parent. The wallet is `deterministic(account_id, seed, vault)` — the same wallet `Bearer near:` reaches for that account, seed and vault.

### Response (both modes)

```json
{
  "wallet_id": "uuid-string",
  "near_account_id": "hex64-implicit-account",
  "vault_id": "vault.example.near"
}
```

`vault_id` is present only for a vault-scoped wallet.

## DELETE /wallet/v1/api-key/:key_hash — revoke a key

Revokes one `wk_` key of the authenticated wallet. Auth: any credential of that wallet (`Bearer near:...` or `Bearer wk_...`). The key stops working at once. Response: `{"revoked": true}`.

**The last active key cannot be revoked** (409 Conflict), so a wallet reachable only through `wk_` keys cannot lock itself out. The rule counts `wk_` keys only: a deterministic wallet with a single delegate key cannot revoke it, even though its account can still sign `Bearer near:` requests.

### Sub-agent usage

```python
# Parent: derive the key (no storage needed, re-derive any time)
api_key = "wk_" + hmac.new(NEAR_SECRET, f"{seed}:0".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

# Parent: register its hash (idempotent)
requests.put(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/api-key", json={
    "account_id": ACCOUNT_ID, "seed": "sub-task-42",
    "key_hash": hashlib.sha256(api_key.encode()).hexdigest(),
    "pubkey": NEAR_PUBKEY, "message": message, "signature": sig,
})

# Sub-agent: plain Bearer token
requests.get(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/balance",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"})
```

## Summary of endpoints

| Endpoint | Auth | Creates wallet? | Returns api_key? | Use case |
|----------|------|----------------|-----------------|----------|
| `POST /register` (no body) | None | Yes (random) | Yes (`wk_`) | Quick start, testing |
| `POST /register` (with signature) | NEAR sig in body | Yes (deterministic) | No | Server/bot that then uses `Bearer near:...` |
| any `/wallet/v1/*` with `Bearer near:` | NEAR sig in header | Yes, on first use | No | Every request of a deterministic client |
| `PUT /wallet/v1/api-key` | Bearer header OR NEAR sig in body | Yes if needed | No (caller knows it) | Register a delegate key for a sub-agent |
| `DELETE /wallet/v1/api-key/:key_hash` | `Bearer near:...` or `Bearer wk_...` | No | — | Revoke a key (last key protected) |

## Auth signatures from the wallet's own key — POST /wallet/v1/auth-sign

To produce OutLayer's `Bearer near:` / register / api-key auth signature **with the wallet's TEE key** (rather than a NEAR key you hold), call `POST /wallet/v1/auth-sign`.

Request body: `{ "purpose": "bearer" | "register" | "api-key", "seed": "...", "vault_id": "..." }` (`vault_id` only for `bearer`). The keystore builds the exact domain-separated string with a fresh server timestamp and signs it raw ed25519. It moves no funds, so it is allowed on any wallet that is not frozen. Response:

```json
{
  "auth_message": "auth:<seed>:<timestamp>",
  "auth_timestamp": 1712000000,
  "signature": "<base58, no ed25519: prefix>",
  "public_key": "ed25519:<base58>"
}
```

Send `auth_message` verbatim. `POST /wallet/v1/sign-message` produces NEP-413 signatures only and does not sign raw bytes. It never signs for an intents verifier (`intents.near`, `intents.far`), and under a policy only for the recipients listed in `capabilities.sign_message.allowed_recipients`.

## Flow examples

All Python examples share the helpers defined in Flow 2: `_sign_message()`, `_make_bearer()`, `NEAR_SECRET`, `NEAR_PUBKEY`, `ACCOUNT_ID`, `API_BASE`. Flows 6 and 7 also use:

```python
def wallet_request_by_seed(seed: str, method: str, path: str, **kwargs):
    """Wallet API call using Bearer near:... for a specific seed."""
    return requests.request(method, f"{API_BASE}{path}",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {_make_bearer(seed)}"},
        **kwargs,
    )
```

### Flow 1: Quick start (random wallet)

No NEAR account needed.

```python
# 1. Register — one call, no auth
resp = requests.post("https://api.outlayer.ai/register")
api_key = resp.json()["api_key"]          # "wk_a1b2c3..."
account = resp.json()["near_account_id"]  # "hex64..."

# 2. Use the wallet — plain Bearer token
requests.get("https://api.outlayer.ai/wallet/v1/balance",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"})
```

The developer stores `api_key`. The coordinator keeps only its SHA-256 hash; a lost key cannot be recovered.

---

### Flow 2: Telegram bot (deterministic, NEAR signature auth)

The bot holds one full-access NEAR key in env and creates wallets for any number of users, storing nothing per user.

```python
import hashlib, hmac, json, time, base64, requests
from nacl.signing import SigningKey
import base58

# ── Setup (once, in env) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
NEAR_SECRET = load_near_secret_bytes()          # 32-byte ed25519 seed of a full-access key
NEAR_KEY = SigningKey(NEAR_SECRET)
NEAR_PUBKEY = f"ed25519:{base58.b58encode(NEAR_KEY.verify_key.encode()).decode()}"
ACCOUNT_ID = "my-tg-bot.near"
API_BASE = "https://api.outlayer.ai"

# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _sign_message(message: str) -> str:
    """Sign a message with the bot's NEAR key, return base58 signature."""
    return base58.b58encode(NEAR_KEY.sign(message.encode()).signature).decode()

def _seed_for_user(telegram_user_id: int) -> str:
    """Deterministic seed from user ID. Same user → same seed → same wallet."""
    return hashlib.sha256(str(telegram_user_id).encode()).hexdigest()

def _make_bearer(seed: str) -> str:
    """Build the Bearer near:... token for one wallet API call."""
    timestamp = int(time.time())
    message = f"auth:{seed}:{timestamp}"
    payload = json.dumps({
        "account_id": ACCOUNT_ID,
        "seed": seed,
        "pubkey": NEAR_PUBKEY,
        "timestamp": timestamp,
        "signature": _sign_message(message),
    }, separators=(",", ":"))
    token = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(payload.encode()).decode().rstrip("=")
    return f"near:{token}"

# ── Registration (idempotent — safe on every /start) ──────────────────
def ensure_wallet_with_seed(seed: str) -> dict:
    timestamp = int(time.time())
    message = f"register:{seed}:{timestamp}"
    resp = requests.post(f"{API_BASE}/register", json={
        "account_id": ACCOUNT_ID,
        "seed": seed,
        "pubkey": NEAR_PUBKEY,
        "message": message,
        "signature": _sign_message(message),
    })
    return resp.json()
    # First call:  creates the wallet, returns { wallet_id, near_account_id, trial }
    # Repeat call: returns the same wallet

def ensure_wallet(telegram_user_id: int) -> dict:
    return ensure_wallet_with_seed(_seed_for_user(telegram_user_id))

# ── Wallet operations (Bearer near:... on every request) ─────────────
def wallet_request(telegram_user_id: int, method: str, path: str, **kwargs):
    seed = _seed_for_user(telegram_user_id)
    return requests.request(method, f"{API_BASE}{path}",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {_make_bearer(seed)}"},
        **kwargs,
    )

# ── Bot handlers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def on_start(user_id: int):
    wallet = ensure_wallet(user_id)
    send_message(user_id, f"Your wallet: {wallet['near_account_id']}")

def on_balance(user_id: int):
    resp = wallet_request(user_id, "GET", "/wallet/v1/balance")
    send_message(user_id, f"Balance: {resp.json()}")

def on_swap(user_id: int, token_in: str, token_out: str, amount_in: str):
    resp = wallet_request(user_id, "POST", "/wallet/v1/intents/swap", json={
        "token_in": token_in,      # e.g. "nep141:wrap.near"
        "token_out": token_out,    # e.g. "nep141:usdt.tether-token.near"
        "amount_in": amount_in,    # smallest units
    })
    send_message(user_id, f"Swap: {resp.json()}")

def on_send(user_id: int, receiver: str, amount_yocto: str):
    resp = wallet_request(user_id, "POST", "/wallet/v1/transfer", json={
        "to": receiver,
        "amount": amount_yocto,
    })
    send_message(user_id, f"Sent: {resp.json()}")
```

The bot stores no per-user keys. Restart, redeploy, move servers — everything keeps working. The NEAR key in env is the only secret, and it is a full-access key of the bot's account: keep the account for this purpose only.

---

### Flow 3: Web app with Google login (deterministic, NEAR signature auth)

Same as the bot, with the seed derived from the OAuth provider and user ID.

```python
def on_google_login(google_user_id: str) -> dict:
    seed = hashlib.sha256(f"google:{google_user_id}".encode()).hexdigest()
    return ensure_wallet_with_seed(seed)

def on_github_login(github_user_id: str) -> dict:
    seed = hashlib.sha256(f"github:{github_user_id}".encode()).hexdigest()
    return ensure_wallet_with_seed(seed)

# Different provider + same person = different wallets (by design)
# Same provider + same person = always the same wallet
```

The seed is a hex digest, so it satisfies the seed alphabet whatever the provider's IDs contain.

---

### Flow 4a: Custody wallet creating sub-agents (Bearer auth, no NEAR key)

The parent has a `wk_` API key and no NEAR key.

```python
import hashlib, requests

API = "https://api.outlayer.ai"
PARENT_KEY = "wk_..."
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {PARENT_KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

def create_sub_agent_wallet(task_id: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    seed = f"sub-agent-{task_id}"
    sub_key = f"wk_{hashlib.sha256(f'{seed}:0:{PARENT_KEY}'.encode()).hexdigest()}"
    key_hash = hashlib.sha256(sub_key.encode()).hexdigest()

    resp = requests.put(f"{API}/wallet/v1/api-key",
        headers=HEADERS,
        json={"seed": seed, "key_hash": key_hash},
    ).json()
    return resp["near_account_id"], sub_key

account, key = create_sub_agent_wallet("task-42")
# Sub-agent uses: Authorization: Bearer wk_...
```

A parent registered with `vault_id` passes its vault to every sub-wallet.

---

### Flow 4b: NEAR account creating sub-agents (NEAR signature)

The parent holds a NEAR key; sub-agents get plain Bearer tokens.

```python
def create_sub_agent_wallet(task_id: str, key_index: int = 0) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Create the wallet + derive a wk_ key for a sub-agent.
    Returns (near_account_id, api_key). Call again to re-derive."""

    seed = f"sub-agent-{task_id}"

    # 1. Derive the wk_ key deterministically
    key_material = hmac.new(
        NEAR_SECRET, f"{seed}:{key_index}".encode(), hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()
    api_key = f"wk_{key_material}"
    key_hash = hashlib.sha256(api_key.encode()).hexdigest()

    # 2. Register its hash (idempotent)
    timestamp = int(time.time())
    message = f"api-key:{seed}:{timestamp}"
    resp = requests.put(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/api-key", json={
        "account_id": ACCOUNT_ID,
        "seed": seed,
        "key_hash": key_hash,
        "pubkey": NEAR_PUBKEY,
        "message": message,
        "signature": _sign_message(message),
    })
    return resp.json()["near_account_id"], api_key

account, key = create_sub_agent_wallet("task-42")
sub_agent = spawn_agent(task="Buy 10 USDT on NEAR", wallet_key=key)

# ── Sub-agent (no crypto, any language) ───────────────────────────────
def sub_agent_main(wallet_key: str):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {wallet_key}"}
    balance = requests.get(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/balance", headers=headers).json()
    swap = requests.post(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/intents/swap", headers=headers, json={
        "token_in": "nep141:wrap.near",
        "token_out": "nep141:usdt.tether-token.near",
        "amount_in": "10000000000000000000000000",   # 10 wNEAR
    }).json()

# ── Later: the parent re-derives the key without any storage ─────────
_, same_key = create_sub_agent_wallet("task-42")  # same key as before
```

The sub-agent's wallet here is the wallet `Bearer near:` reaches for `(ACCOUNT_ID, "sub-agent-task-42")`, so the parent can operate it directly too.

---

### Flow 5: NEAR key rotation

The bot's NEAR key was exposed. Rotate without affecting wallets.

```bash
near generate-key --outputDir ./new-key
near add-key my-tg-bot.near ed25519:NEW_PUBLIC_KEY      # full access
# Update the bot's env with the new key, restart the bot
near delete-key my-tg-bot.near ed25519:OLD_PUBLIC_KEY
# Within 60 s, Bearer near: tokens signed by the old key → 401
```

Wallets are not affected — `wallet_id` depends on `(account_id, seed)`, not on the key.

**For Flow 4b:** existing `wk_` keys keep working after a rotation (they are stored by hash, independent of the NEAR key), but the parent derived them with the old key and can no longer re-derive them. Sub-agents created afterwards use keys derived from the new key. Old sub-agent keys stay valid until revoked.

---

### Flow 6: Key revocation (compromised key)

```bash
near delete-key my-tg-bot.near ed25519:COMPROMISED_KEY
# - Bearer near: signed by the compromised key → 401 within 60 s
# - wk_ keys derived from it → still work (stored by hash)
```

To revoke the `wk_` delegate keys derived from the compromised key:

```python
for seed, index in compromised_sub_agents:
    old_key = "wk_" + hmac.new(OLD_NEAR_SECRET, f"{seed}:{index}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    old_hash = hashlib.sha256(old_key.encode()).hexdigest()
    # Authenticated with the new NEAR key
    wallet_request_by_seed(seed, "DELETE", f"/wallet/v1/api-key/{old_hash}")
```

Register the replacement key first: the last active `wk_` key of a wallet cannot be revoked (409).

---

### Flow 7: Sub-agent with a policy (spending limits)

The parent creates a wallet for the sub-agent that may only swap wNEAR, at most 5 wNEAR per swap. Setting a policy is three steps: encrypt it, have the wallet sign it for the account that will store it, store it on chain.

```python
# ── Parent agent ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# 1. Create the wallet + wk_ key for the sub-agent (Flow 4b)
account, sub_key = create_sub_agent_wallet("task-42")
seed = "sub-agent-task-42"
wallet_id = wallet_request_by_seed(seed, "GET", "/wallet/v1/address?chain=near").json()["wallet_id"]

# 2. Encrypt the policy in the keystore
encrypted = wallet_request_by_seed(seed, "POST", "/wallet/v1/encrypt-policy", json={
    "wallet_id": wallet_id,
    "rules": {
        "transaction_types": ["swap"],
        "limits": {"per_transaction": {"nep141:wrap.near": "5000000000000000000000000"}},
    },
    "capabilities": {"swap": {"allowed": True}},
}).json()                                # { encrypted_base64, wallet_pubkey }

# 3. Have the wallet sign it for the account that will store it.
#    `caller` is part of what is signed: the answer works for that account only.
signed = wallet_request_by_seed(seed, "POST", "/wallet/v1/sign-policy", json={
    "encrypted_data": encrypted["encrypted_base64"],
    "caller": "you.near",
}).json()                                # { signature_hex, public_key_hex }

# 4. you.near calls store_wallet_policy on outlayer.near with a storage deposit
#    (estimate_wallet_policy_cost gives the amount):
#      { "wallet_pubkey": encrypted["wallet_pubkey"],
#        "encrypted_data": encrypted["encrypted_base64"],
#        "wallet_signature": signed["signature_hex"] }
#    you.near becomes the policy's controller: only it can update, freeze or delete it.

# 5. Hand the wk_ key to the sub-agent
sub_agent = spawn_agent(task="Buy USDT", wallet_key=sub_key)

# ── Sub-agent ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {sub_key}"}

requests.get(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/balance", headers=headers)          # reads are not policy-gated

requests.post(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/intents/swap", headers=headers, json={
    "token_in": "nep141:wrap.near", "token_out": "nep141:usdt.tether-token.near",
    "amount_in": "3000000000000000000000000",                          # 3 wNEAR: allowed
})

requests.post(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/intents/swap", headers=headers, json={
    "token_in": "nep141:wrap.near", "token_out": "nep141:usdt.tether-token.near",
    "amount_in": "10000000000000000000000000",                         # 10 wNEAR
})  # → 403 policy_denied (per-transaction limit)

requests.post(f"{API_BASE}/wallet/v1/transfer", headers=headers, json={
    "to": "attacker.near", "amount": "100",
})  # → 403 policy_denied (transfer is not an allowed transaction type)
```

The keystore evaluates the policy inside the TEE before it signs; the sub-agent's key cannot bypass it. The cumulative limits (daily, hourly, monthly, rate limit) are counted by the coordinator. The controller account changes the policy, or freezes the wallet, with a transaction of its own. The policy format is documented at https://app.outlayer.ai/docs/agent-custody.

---

> Source: https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/PAYMENT_CHECKS.md

# Payment Checks

Gasless agent-to-agent payments through ephemeral NEAR Intents accounts. Agent A locks tokens from its intents balance into a check and sends a single key to Agent B, who claims the funds into its own wallet — no gas, no on-chain account, no exchange of wallet keys. Supports partial claims, expiry, and reclaim.

Payment checks run on NEAR Intents, which is mainnet only: on testnet every endpoint answers 503. The website reference is https://app.outlayer.ai/docs/payment-checks.

## Why Payment Checks

| Problem | Payment Checks Solution |
|---------|------------------------|
| Direct transfers require NEAR for gas | Create, claim and reclaim are gasless — solver relay with off-chain NEP-413 signatures |
| Receiver needs an on-chain account with gas | Receiver needs only an OutLayer wallet credential |
| Direct transfers are irreversible | Sender can reclaim unclaimed funds at any time |
| No native partial payment support | Built-in partial claim and partial reclaim |
| Escrow requires smart contract development | A check acts as lightweight escrow — one API call |

## How It Works

```
Agent A (Sender)              Agent B (Receiver)
     |                              |
     |  1. POST /create             |
     |  ────────────────►           |
     |  ← check_key                 |
     |                              |
     |  2. Send check_key           |
     |  ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─►|
     |     (any channel)            |
     |                              |
     |                 3. POST /peek |
     |                 (verify)      |
     |                              |
     |                4. POST /claim |
     |                ◄─────────────|
     |                 funds move    |
     |                              |
     |  5. POST /reclaim (optional) |
     |  (get unclaimed funds back)  |
```

### Step-by-step

1. **Create** — Agent A calls `POST /wallet/v1/payment-check/create`. The tokens must already be in A's intents balance (`POST /wallet/v1/intents/deposit` or a cross-chain deposit). The keystore derives a unique ephemeral key, the wallet signs a transfer of the tokens from its intents balance to the ephemeral account, the coordinator publishes it to the solver relay, and the response carries the `check_key`.

2. **Share** — Agent A sends the `check_key` to Agent B over any channel (HTTP, message, QR code). The key is a 64-char hex string.

3. **Peek** (optional) — Agent B calls `POST /wallet/v1/payment-check/peek` with the key to read the check's balance, memo, status and expiry before claiming.

4. **Claim** — Agent B calls `POST /wallet/v1/payment-check/claim` with the key. The coordinator signs, with the `check_key`, a transfer intent from the ephemeral account to Agent B's intents balance and publishes it. Supports partial claims.

5. **Reclaim** (optional) — Agent A can reclaim unclaimed funds via `POST /wallet/v1/payment-check/reclaim`. The keystore derives the ephemeral key again, so A does not need to store it.

## Transfer Mechanism

Every leg is a NEAR Intents `transfer` intent: the coordinator gets a NEP-413 signature and submits it to the solver relay, which executes it on `intents.near`. Nothing pays gas.

| Operation | From → To | Who Signs | Gas |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----|
| Create | Sender's intents balance → ephemeral account | Sender's wallet key (keystore TEE) | None |
| Claim | Ephemeral account → claimer's intents balance | The `check_key`, used by the coordinator | None |
| Reclaim | Ephemeral account → sender's intents balance | The ephemeral key, derived again by the keystore and used by the coordinator | None |

### Ephemeral Accounts

Each check gets its own account on `intents.near`, derived from the wallet's master secret and a per-wallet counter. This gives each check an isolated balance that can be moved by whoever holds the `check_key`, or by the sender through a reclaim.

```
Key derivation (HMAC-SHA256 with the wallet's master, inside the keystore):
  wallet:{id}:near                        ← main wallet key (never exported)
  wallet:{id}:near:check:{counter}        ← ephemeral key per check

The check_key IS the raw ed25519 private key of the ephemeral account.
The ephemeral account ID = hex(public_key) on intents.near.
```

A wallet bound to a per-customer vault derives its check keys from the vault's master.

## Policy

Under a stored policy, creating a check needs `capabilities.payment_check.allowed = true` (default-DENY), and the check's token and amount are held to the policy's per-transaction limit. A check routes funds to whoever holds its key, so a recipient whitelist cannot gate it; the capability is the gate. A wallet with no policy can create checks freely.

The create message is supplied by the coordinator, not built by the enclave: see [Limits we state plainly](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md#11-limits-we-state-plainly).

## API Reference

Base URL: `https://api.outlayer.ai/wallet/v1/payment-check`

Every endpoint takes a wallet credential: `Authorization: Bearer wk_...` or `Authorization: Bearer near:...`.

### Retries and timeouts

Send `X-Idempotency-Key` on create, batch-create, claim and reclaim, and `X-Answer-Within: <seconds>` below your own timeout. A call whose transfer is not confirmed in time answers with an in-flight status and a `poll_url`; poll it rather than repeating the call. A repeated call with the same idempotency key answers `duplicate_idempotency_key` naming the earlier request; for a create it carries `checks: [{check_id, check_key, status}]` with the key derived again (`check_key: null` when asked under a different vault scope than the create's).

### POST /create

Create a new payment check.

**Request:**
```json
{
  "token": "17208628f84f5d6ad33f0da3bbbeb27ffcb398eac501a31bd6ad2011e36133a1",
  "amount": "1000000",
  "memo": "Payment for data analysis",
  "expires_in": 3600
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `token` | string | yes | Token contract ID (e.g., the USDC contract) |
| `amount` | string | yes | Amount in smallest units (e.g., "1000000" = 1 USDC), greater than 0 |
| `memo` | string | no | Optional memo (max 256 chars), visible to the receiver |
| `expires_in` | number | no | Expiry in seconds from now, at most ten years |

**Response:**
```json
{
  "check_id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "check_key": "7f3a9b2c...64 hex chars...",
  "status": "unclaimed",
  "token": "17208628f84f5d6ad33f0da3bbbeb27ffcb398eac501a31bd6ad2011e36133a1",
  "amount": "1000000",
  "memo": "Payment for data analysis",
  "created_at": "2026-03-13T10:00:00Z",
  "expires_at": "2026-03-13T11:00:00Z"
}
```

`status` is `unclaimed` once the funding transfer has executed, or `creating` with a `poll_url` while it is unconfirmed. The `check_key` is in both answers: keep it, and do not create the check again. A `creating` check ends `unclaimed`, or `failed` if the funding never executed (nothing moved).

### POST /batch-create

Create up to 10 checks in one call, each with its own key and ephemeral account.

**Request:**
```json
{
  "checks": [
    {"token": "170...a1", "amount": "1000000", "memo": "Task 1"},
    {"token": "170...a1", "amount": "2000000", "memo": "Task 2"}
  ]
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "checks": [
    {"check_id": "...", "check_key": "...", "status": "unclaimed", "token": "...", "amount": "1000000", ...},
    {"check_id": "...", "check_key": "...", "status": "unclaimed", "token": "...", "amount": "2000000", ...}
  ]
}
```

If the batch stops before its last check, the response carries `error`: the checks listed were created, the rest were not.

### POST /claim

Claim funds from a check into the caller's wallet. Supports partial claims.

**Request:**
```json
{
  "check_key": "7f3a9b2c...64 hex chars...",
  "amount": "500000"
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `check_key` | string | yes | The 64-char hex key from the sender |
| `amount` | string | no | Partial claim amount (omit to claim the whole balance) |

**Response:**
```json
{
  "request_id": "5e6f7a8b-...",
  "status": "partially_claimed",
  "token": "17208628f84f5d6ad33f0da3bbbeb27ffcb398eac501a31bd6ad2011e36133a1",
  "amount_claimed": "500000",
  "remaining": "500000",
  "memo": "Payment for data analysis",
  "claimed_at": "2026-03-13T10:05:00Z",
  "intent_hash": "Bx7k..."
}
```

`status` is `claimed` / `partially_claimed`, or `processing` with a `poll_url` (and no `remaining` / `claimed_at`) while the transfer is unconfirmed. A claim is refused after the check's expiry, while the check is still being funded or another leg is in flight, and once it is fully claimed or reclaimed. Only checks created through OutLayer can be claimed.

### POST /reclaim

Reclaim unclaimed funds to the sender's wallet. Only the wallet that created the check can reclaim; expiry does not prevent it.

**Request:**
```json
{
  "check_id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "amount": "500000"
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `check_id` | string | yes | The check ID from the create response |
| `amount` | string | no | Partial reclaim amount (omit to reclaim the whole balance) |

**Response:**
```json
{
  "request_id": "9c0d1e2f-...",
  "status": "reclaimed",
  "token": "17208628f84f5d6ad33f0da3bbbeb27ffcb398eac501a31bd6ad2011e36133a1",
  "amount_reclaimed": "500000",
  "remaining": "0",
  "reclaimed_at": "2026-03-13T10:10:00Z",
  "intent_hash": "Cx9m..."
}
```

`status` is `reclaimed` / `partially_reclaimed`, or `processing` with a `poll_url`.

### GET /status?check_id=...

Current state of a check. Only the creating wallet can query it.

**Response:**
```json
{
  "check_id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "token": "17208628f84f5d6ad33f0da3bbbeb27ffcb398eac501a31bd6ad2011e36133a1",
  "amount": "1000000",
  "claimed_amount": "500000",
  "reclaimed_amount": "500000",
  "status": "reclaimed",
  "memo": "Payment for data analysis",
  "created_at": "2026-03-13T10:00:00Z",
  "expires_at": "2026-03-13T11:00:00Z",
  "claimed_at": "2026-03-13T10:05:00Z",
  "claimed_by": "a2b3b5b5c72c..."
}
```

### GET /list?status=...&limit=50&offset=0

List the checks created by the authenticated wallet.

| Param | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `status` | no | Filter: `creating`, `unclaimed`, `claiming`, `partially_claimed`, `claimed`, `reclaiming`, `partially_reclaimed`, `reclaimed`, `failed`, `expired` |
| `limit` | no | Max results (default 50, max 100) |
| `offset` | no | Pagination offset (default 0) |

### POST /peek

Read a check's balance using its `check_key`, to verify it before claiming. Any wallet credential can peek.

**Request:**
```json
{
  "check_key": "7f3a9b2c...64 hex chars..."
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "token": "17208628f84f5d6ad33f0da3bbbeb27ffcb398eac501a31bd6ad2011e36133a1",
  "balance": "1000000",
  "memo": "Payment for data analysis",
  "status": "unclaimed",
  "expires_at": "2026-03-13T11:00:00Z"
}
```

`balance` is read from `intents.near`.

## Check Lifecycle

```
                    create
                      |
                      v
                  [creating] ---- funding never executed ---> [failed]
                      |
                      v
                  [unclaimed]
                   /      \
          claim   /        \  reclaim
                 v          v
       [partially_claimed] [partially_reclaimed]
              |       \         /       |
       claim  |        \       /        | reclaim
              v         v     v         v
          [claimed]   (mixed)    [reclaimed]
```

**Statuses:**
- `creating` — funding transfer not confirmed yet
- `unclaimed` — funds locked, waiting to be claimed
- `claiming` / `reclaiming` — a claim or reclaim is in flight; another waits for it
- `partially_claimed` — some funds claimed, rest available
- `partially_reclaimed` — some funds reclaimed by the sender
- `claimed` — the balance reached zero through a claim
- `reclaimed` — the balance reached zero through a reclaim
- `failed` — the funding never executed; nothing moved
- `expired` — reported for an `unclaimed` check past its expiry

**Expiry:** if `expires_in` is set, the check cannot be claimed after expiry. The funds stay in the ephemeral account until the sender reclaims them; expiry does not return them by itself.

## Security

| Threat | Mitigation |
|--------|------------|
| check_key intercepted in transit | Use encrypted channels (HTTPS, E2E messaging). A leaked key lets anyone with an OutLayer wallet claim the funds. |
| Sender's API key compromised | The API key can be revoked. Under a policy, checks need the `payment_check` capability and stay within the per-transaction limit. |
| Replay of claim/reclaim | Each intent has a random nonce and a 5-minute deadline; `intents.near` rejects a reused nonce. Amounts are tracked under a row lock. |
| Ephemeral key collision | Per-wallet counter, incremented atomically in the database; a counter value is never reused. |
| Funds stuck in ephemeral account | The sender can always reclaim — the keystore derives the ephemeral key again from the same path. |

**Who sees the `check_key`:** it never goes on chain. It is returned by the keystore through the coordinator on create, and on claim the receiver sends it to the coordinator, which signs the claim with it outside the TEE. Because the keystore can derive any check's key for the coordinator, the coordinator is trusted with every open check's balance; see [NON_CUSTODIAL.md](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md).

## Comparison

|  | Payment Checks | Direct Transfer | Smart Contract Escrow |
|--|----------------|-----------------|----------------------|
| Gas required | None (funds must be in the intents balance) | Sender pays | Both parties pay |
| Receiver needs account | Only an OutLayer wallet credential | On-chain account + gas | On-chain account + gas |
| Partial payment | Built-in | N/A | Custom logic |
| Reclaim | Built-in, gasless | N/A (irreversible) | Custom logic + gas |
| On-chain footprint | Intents executed by the solver relay | 1 transaction | Contract deployment + calls |
| Setup complexity | One API call | One API call | Contract dev + deployment |

## Use Cases

- **Agent-to-agent payments** — Agent A creates a check and sends the key with its API request. Agent B verifies it (peek), does the work, claims payment. If B does not deliver, A reclaims.
- **Bounties & task rewards** — Create a check with an expiry and share the key with the task completer. Partial claims allow splitting among contributors.
- **Escrow-style payments** — Lock funds in a check and share the key only when conditions are met.
- **Batch payouts** — `batch-create` makes up to 10 checks in one call, each with its own key.

---

# Agent Custody: Outlayer (TEE) vs. TLA active-signer (on-chain MPC)

A side-by-side of the two custody models, followed by notes on each point.
The two are built for different jobs; this is meant to make the trade-offs
visible, not to declare a winner. The OutLayer column describes OutLayer's
code. The `active-signer` column describes that design as it was presented
to us; its figures are our estimates, not measurements.

## Comparison

| Dimension | Outlayer custody (TEE) | TLA `active-signer` (on-chain MPC) |
|---|---|---|
| Trust root | Intel TDX enclave, remotely attested (Intel DCAP / PCS), plus OutLayer's coordinator and, at this stage, OutLayer-held governance keys &nbsp;\* | NEAR MPC network + on-chain `active-signer` contract |
| Where the key lives | Derived on demand inside the keystore enclave from a master secret; never stored, no endpoint exports it. Stage caveat: the DAO account's full-access key can obtain the shared master outside an enclave | Held by no one — threshold-shared across MPC nodes |
| Producing a signature | One coordinator → keystore round trip, which includes one RPC view read of the on-chain policy; no transaction, no MPC round | Signer call + MPC yield/resume, multi-block (~2–6 s, estimate) |
| Overhead per signed action | None beyond the action's own transaction or intent | Signer function-call + MPC round + broadcast, on top of the action |
| Gas to produce a signature | None | ~0.003–0.008 NEAR/sig (estimate) |
| Chains from one custody | NEAR (ed25519), Solana (ed25519), EVM (secp256k1, one address on every EVM chain) | NEAR — `active-signer` builds NEAR transactions |
| Account onboarding | Implicit account — no `create_account` / `add_key` and no `intents.near` key registration | Named account — MPC-derive + `create_account` + `add_key` + funding for storage, **plus** `add_public_key` on `intents.near`, all on chain per agent |
| Concurrency | Money-moving operations on one wallet are serialized by the coordinator (velocity limits, NEAR nonces); separate wallets run in parallel | Per-account nonce commit serializes actions |
| Action set | Programmable policy: capabilities, limits, whitelists, approvals, reject-if-transaction guards | `function_call` + `transfer` only, enforced at the type level |
| Ownership transfer / resale | Not a native primitive | Native — compare-and-swap of the operating key |
| Built-in recovery | Of the custody root: per-customer vaults with a unilateral exit (testnet). Of an agent's authority: by composition | Native policy engine — timelock, watcher quorum, attestation |
| Human-readable identity | Implicit hex by default | Named (TLA sub-account, e.g. `agent.claude`) |
| Verifiability of authority | Remote attestation of the measured code; on-chain approval of measurements | On-chain contract logic + MPC network |

\* Both models root in MPC; the difference is *when* and *how often*.
OutLayer's wallet keys are derived (HMAC-SHA256) from a master secret that the
keystore obtains from the NEAR MPC network through an on-chain `request_key`
call on the DAO contract, which only an approved, attested keystore's access
key can make. The shared root is obtained when the keystore starts; a
per-customer vault's master is obtained through the customer's own vault
contract when the keystore first serves that vault. From then on the keystore
signs locally, with no MPC call per action. The `active-signer` model calls
MPC (`v1.signer`) on **every** signature. So it is not "TEE vs MPC": it is one
MPC derivation per master versus one MPC round-trip per signed action.

The master stays in enclave memory, with one exception at this stage:
`dao.outlayer.near` carries a full-access key, and a transaction signed with it
passes the `request_key` check, so its holder can obtain the shared master
outside any enclave. See
[Governance at this stage](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md#governance-at-this-stage).

Ownership transfer, a built-in recovery engine for an agent's authority, and
human-readable names are first-class in the TLA model and not native to
OutLayer custody. Signing cost, signing latency, chain coverage and onboarding
are where the TEE model is stronger, and they come from one thing: signing is
local, not an on-chain round-trip. Concurrency is not a difference: both
serialize per account.

## Notes

### Latency and cost per action

OutLayer signs inside the keystore enclave, with no transaction and no gas to
produce the signature. The keystore reads the wallet's encrypted policy from
the chain (a view call, free) before it signs. The on-chain-signer + MPC path
pays, for **every** signed action, a function-call transaction into the signer
contract, an MPC signing round (yield / resume across several blocks), and a
broadcast. Both models pay the underlying transaction's own gas when the action
hits the chain; the difference is the signing overhead layered on top. At
wallet cadence — a few transactions a day — that overhead is negligible. At
agent cadence — many actions a minute — it dominates.

End to end, an OutLayer operation that moves money also waits for its own
settlement (a NEAR transaction, or an intent through the solver relay), which
is seconds, not milliseconds.

**Worked example — an agent doing one action per minute** (1,440 actions/day):

- *TLA `active-signer`:* ~0.003–0.008 NEAR of signing overhead per action →
  roughly **4–12 NEAR/day**, before the underlying transactions' own gas, plus
  the MPC round's latency on every action.
- *Outlayer:* **0 NEAR** of signing overhead. A free-tier wallet has a daily
  ceiling on custody operations; a subscription lifts it.

The `active-signer` figures are estimates — `1 TGas ≈ 0.0001 NEAR` at floor
gas price, tens of TGas burned along the `active-signer` → `v1.signer` →
callback chain (confidence: low–moderate). The point is the order of magnitude
and that the cost accrues **per action**.

### One custody, multiple chains

One wallet signs NEAR (ed25519), Solana (ed25519) and EVM (secp256k1); each
chain family has its own derivation seed, so a signature for one can never be
a signature for another. There is no per-chain signing contract to deploy. For
EVM and Solana the client builds and broadcasts the transaction; the keystore
only signs. The `active-signer` model, as designed, builds NEAR transactions.

### Onboarding: implicit accounts

Agents get NEAR implicit accounts — the account ID *is* the public key — so
there is no `create_account` and no `add_key`. A wallet can receive funds and
act on `intents.near` without any on-chain setup. The named-account model
requires on-chain account creation, funding for storage, and a key install per
agent.

There is a second, intents-specific cost. NEAR Intents authorizes a NEP-413
signature against a public key. For an implicit account the account ID *is*
that key, so Intents derives it directly and nothing needs to be registered.
For a named account the key cannot be inferred from the name, so it must be
registered with `intents.near` via `add_public_key` before Intents will
recognize the account — an extra on-chain call per agent.

### Programmable policy, evaluated next to the key

The keystore enclave that holds the key evaluates the wallet's policy before
every signature: capabilities per primitive (default-deny under a policy),
per-transaction caps, recipient whitelists, time windows, freeze and
multisig approvals. Two parts sit outside the enclave and are trusted to the
coordinator: the cumulative counters (daily, hourly, monthly caps and the
hourly rate limit), and, for five intents operations (swaps, cross-chain
withdrawals, confidential-intents operations, limit orders, payment checks),
the message that is signed. Details:
[Limits we state plainly](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md#11-limits-we-state-plainly).

The `active-signer` model restricts the action set to `function_call` +
`transfer` at the type level, so dangerous actions cannot be expressed at all.
Ours is programmable; theirs is hard-restricted. Different tools for different
risk models.

### Compute and custody on one platform

OutLayer pairs custody with verifiable compute. An agent's logic runs in an
attested TDX worker and its keys are used in an attested TDX keystore; the
worker reaches the wallet through host functions that the coordinator routes
to the keystore. The agent can compute privately and sign the result without
leaving attested hardware, though the two run in separate enclaves with the
coordinator between them. The TLA model is a custody-and-ownership layer; it
has no compute component, and does not need one.

### Concurrency

The coordinator serializes money-moving operations per wallet: the velocity
limits need a consistent read-evaluate-record window, and NEAR transactions
from one account need ordered nonces. A second operation on a busy wallet
waits briefly, then is told `wallet_busy`. Separate wallets do not block each
other, so an agent that needs parallelism spreads it across wallets. The
`active-signer` model serializes per account on its nonce commit. Neither model
signs in parallel for one account.

### Trust assumptions

- OutLayer trusts the Intel TDX hardware and the DCAP / Intel PCS attestation
  chain, plus on-chain approval of the enclave's measurements. It is a
  single-vendor hardware trust root.
- OutLayer's coordinator is trusted for agent custody: it authenticates API
  keys, keeps the cumulative counters and pending approvals, and supplies the
  signed message for five intents operations.
- At this stage governance runs on single keys held by OutLayer: the DAO's
  full-access key, owner-only measurement approval, and contracts upgraded by
  key. See [Governance at this stage](https://github.com/out-layer/outlayer/blob/main/docs/NON_CUSTODIAL.md#governance-at-this-stage).
- The TLA model trusts the NEAR MPC network (threshold, no single holder) and
  the correctness of the `active-signer` contract.

These are different roots — threshold-distributed versus attested hardware
plus an operator — not one strictly stronger than the other. The cost,
chain-coverage and co-located-compute properties above are consequences of
the TEE root; the ownership, recovery and naming primitives are consequences
of the on-chain root.

### Where the two compose

Naming and recovery can sit **on top of** OutLayer custody without changing
the root: OutLayer's wallets are ordinary NEAR implicit accounts, so a policy
layer that targets ordinary NEAR accounts can target them. The sensible split
is one custody root (TEE, for agent-cadence signing) with a policy layer —
naming, ownership, recovery — composing above it.

---
